notes: Residential range hoods / ventilation hoods. Includes wall-mount, island, undercabinet, and insert/liner types. Each installation type scored identically — the unit of scoring is the ventilation system (blower + capture + filtration), not the housing style. Ductless/recirculating-only products scored but flagged as fundamentally different ventilation approach.

tier_anchors.notes: Vent-A-Hood: Heritage brand since 1933, Houston TX. Patented Magic Lung centrifugal blower captures grease before fan — blower stays clean, extends motor life indefinitely. Whisper-quiet operation. All stainless construction. USA-manufactured. Industry professionals consider Vent-A-Hood the 'Sub-Zero of range hoods.' Wolf: Sub-Zero/Wolf ecosystem. Internal centrifugal blower, stainless baffle filters, pairs with Wolf ranges. Fitchburg WI manufacturing. 2-year full warranty.

Zephyr: San Francisco-based. Appeared 26 times in luxury listings — significant market presence. External/remote blower option (BLB series) enables high CFM with low noise at hood. Stainless baffle filters. LED lighting. Good design + strong performance. Thermador: BSH platform. Integrated with Thermador cooking products. Blower included. BSH parts network provides reliable service ecosystem.

Broan-NuTone volume player's premium line. Stainless construction, adequate CFM (650), mesh filters (aluminum), LED lighting. Competent performance but lacks the blower engineering and build quality of Tier 1-2. Nortek parent company. Broad parts availability through standard retail channels.

Builder-grade floor. Painted steel body, 210 CFM, ~6.5 sones at max, aluminum mesh filters, incandescent lighting. The hood installed in every tract home. Barely adequate ventilation for a standard 30-inch range. Cannot ventilate a pro-style range at all.
No calibration products. Reserved for ductless-only hoods with no real ventilation capability, products with active safety recalls, or unbranded imports with no UL listing.

quality.notes: 304 stainless (18/8 chromium-nickel) is the premium standard — resists corrosion, heat, and cooking acids. 430 stainless (ferritic, magnetic) is adequate but less corrosion-resistant. Painted steel is builder-grade — will chip, discolor, and corrode over time in a high-heat, high-grease environment. Body gauge matters: 18-gauge is premium, 22-gauge is builder.

Vent-A-Hood's centrifugal capture eliminates traditional filters entirely — grease is captured by centrifugal force before reaching the blower. Stainless baffle filters are the premium standard: capture grease efficiently, dishwasher safe, last indefinitely. Aluminum baffle is adequate. Aluminum mesh clogs quickly, deforms in dishwasher, needs frequent replacement. Charcoal = recirculating only, not true ventilation.

Welded seamless construction eliminates grease traps at joints — easier to clean, stronger. Standard welded is adequate. Riveted/assembled panels create grease accumulation points and are weaker under thermal cycling.

LED dimmable with high CRI and adequate lux is the modern standard — 50,000+ hour life, no heat contribution. Halogen gives excellent light quality but adds heat and burns out frequently. Incandescent is builder-grade — short life, high heat, poor energy efficiency.

Centrifugal blowers (squirrel-cage design with ball bearings) move more air at lower noise and last longer than axial fans. Vent-A-Hood Magic Lung and Wolf blowers are centrifugal. Axial fans are cheaper but louder, less efficient, and wear faster. Mixed-flow is a compromise design. The blower is the heart of the hood — this is the range hood equivalent of the cartridge in faucets.

Same rule as all categories. Vent-A-Hood (+1, Houston TX since 1933). Wolf (+1, Fitchburg WI / Sub-Zero ecosystem). Zephyr (0, designed in SF, manufactured in China — disclosed). BSH (0, multi-factory). Broan-NuTone (0, multiple factories identified). Unknown = -1.

performance.notes: CFM (cubic feet per minute) is the primary performance metric. Professional ranges (30,000+ BTU) require minimum 600 CFM; many pros recommend 1 CFM per 100 BTU. A 65,000 BTU Wolf range needs 650+ CFM minimum. Builder-grade hoods at 200 CFM cannot ventilate even a standard 30-inch range during high-heat cooking. HVI-certified CFM ratings are independently verified.

Sone rating measures perceived loudness. 1 sone ≈ quiet refrigerator. 4 sones ≈ normal TV volume. 8+ sones = uncomfortable in open kitchen. HVI-certified sone ratings are independently verified. External/remote blowers can achieve <1 sone at the hood because the motor is remote. Vent-A-Hood centrifugal design achieves ~3 sones at 600 CFM — remarkable for an internal blower.

Capture area should extend at least 3 inches beyond the cooktop on each side for effective capture. A 30-inch hood over a 36-inch range = undersized. Professional installers insist on oversized capture. Island hoods need even larger capture area due to cross-drafts.

Larger duct = lower air resistance = quieter operation at rated CFM. Premium hoods use 10-inch round or equivalent rectangular. Builder-grade uses 6-inch. Undersized ductwork is the #1 installation error that degrades real-world performance below rated specs.

Variable/infinite speed control lets user dial in exact airflow to match cooking. Premium hoods use electronic variable speed or slider controls. 3-speed is adequate for most use cases. 2-speed/single-speed limits usability — either too loud for simmering or inadequate for searing.

External/remote blower option moves the motor outdoors or into the attic — dramatically reduces hood noise while maintaining full CFM. Zephyr BLB series, Broan external blowers. Premium installation option. Not a penalty for not having it — many great hoods use internal blowers. But availability = flexibility for noise-sensitive installations.

durability.notes: Vent-A-Hood offers lifetime motor warranty — reflects confidence in centrifugal design's longevity. Most premium hoods offer 3-year motor warranty. Builder-grade is 1 year. Motor replacement is the most expensive hood repair ($300-800+ with labor).

Centrifugal motors with sealed ball bearings last 20+ years. Vent-A-Hood Magic Lung blowers commonly run 30+ years per owner reports. Sleeve bearings are adequate but wear faster. Axial fans in builder-grade hoods typically last 8-12 years.

Vent-A-Hood centrifugal grease capture keeps the entire internal system clean — grease collects in a removable tray, never reaches blower or ductwork. This extends hood AND duct lifespan. Baffle filters are dishwasher-safe and maintain airflow when clean. Mesh filters clog, reduce airflow, and create fire risk if not cleaned regularly.

Range hoods are mechanically simpler than other appliances — main parts are motor, lights, controls, and filters. Broan-NuTone parts are universally available at any hardware store. Wolf/Vent-A-Hood parts are proprietary but available direct. Some premium European brands have limited US parts availability.

Range hoods are often serviced by general appliance techs or electricians — less brand-specific servicing than dishwashers or refrigerators. Broan-NuTone: any appliance tech. Wolf: factory-certified network. Vent-A-Hood: direct support from Houston factory + authorized dealers. Miele/Thermador: BSH service network.

scoring_rules: Health certs report-only, no composite impact (UL 507 listing, fire suppression)
BSH Platform Rule: Thermador and Bosch hoods may share blower components, controls, or filter designs. Deep dive must confirm. Report must disclose shared platform if confirmed.
Miele Integrated Hood Rule: Miele hoods are designed to pair with Miele ranges but use independent blower systems. Score the hood independently. Report must note integration advantage.
Wolf Pairing Rule: Wolf hoods are designed to pair with Wolf ranges. Score the hood independently but report must note that Wolf recommends specific hood-to-range matching for optimal performance.

Vent-A-Hood Centrifugal Architecture Rule: The Magic Lung centrifugal blower is a fundamentally different ventilation approach. Traditional filter comparisons don't apply. Score the capture efficiency result, not the mechanism.

CFM-to-BTU Matching Rule: Report must include CFM-to-BTU assessment. A hood providing 400 CFM over a 65,000 BTU range is INADEQUATE regardless of build quality. Note: insufficient CFM does not reduce the hood's score (score the product), but the mismatch must be prominently reported.
External Blower Scoring Rule: When external blower is available, score the INTERNAL blower configuration as base. Note external blower option and its performance characteristics in the report.

Ductless/Recirculating Rule: Ductless-only hoods are scored but report must prominently note that recirculating does NOT remove combustion byproducts, moisture, or heat. This is a material ventilation limitation.
Makeup Air Rule: Any hood above 400 CFM may require makeup air system per IRC M1503.4. This is an installation requirement, not a product deficiency. Report as informational.
Score base configuration per Rule 17. Hood + external blower combo vs hood-only are different configurations.
Score the product, not the brand (Rule 19). Different blower sizes under same brand = different products if CFM/sone differ meaningfully.

sources: VACANT — No single dominant independent source for range hoods equivalent to StarCraft (faucets), Karin Kirk (countertops), or Yale (appliances). Yale does not publish hood-specific service rate data. HVI certification provides independent CFM/sone verification but is compliance testing, not comparative analysis.

HVI (Home Ventilating Institute) — independent CFM and sone certification. Industry standard for verified performance specs.

data_sources.notes: HVI certified product directory provides independently verified CFM and sone ratings. Use HVI data as ground truth for any CFM/sone spec claims. Manufacturer-claimed CFM without HVI certification should be treated as unverified.
